Stay out of Excel Hell

Some people swear by the use of Excel shortcuts for everything and worship at the altar of the No Mouse club. I am not one of those people, but I do believe learning some of the most common Excel Shortcuts can save you a lot of time and it is worth learning how to use them even if you still use the mouse for some of your work.

​

Three ways to familiarize yourself with shortcuts.

​

Learn to use the Alt Key

One of the best ways to familiarize yourself with shortcuts in general is by using the ALT key in Excel. The Alt Key will bring up the list of shortcuts for the menu bar. For example, Alt + H brings up the home ribbon and lists all the shortcuts. If you were to Press Alt H + S it would bring up the shortcuts for sorting and you can then press the next letter again.

​

Below is what it would appear on the menu bar if you were to press Alt H S to bring up the options for filtering and sorting your data. If you then pressed S it would sort your data from A to Z.

​

​

​

​

Ask Generative AI (ChatGPT/Claude AI/Bard)

Ask your favorite AI tool to provide you with a list of some of the most common shortcut keys. This is an easy way to get a list of shortcuts that you can start learning. Make a goal to learn one of them every day.

​

Learn from others

The last way to learn is from others. Hundreds if not thousands of people have created shortcut lists, and you can find them all over LinkedIn and the internet. Pick one up today and start learning. Below is a list of some of my favorite shortcuts.

Business Partner's Corner

​

The Power of Active Listening!

​

The great news for Finance professionals (many of us are naturally introverted) is that one of the most powerful, underrated, and underutilized business partnership skills is active listening.

​

Great, generous, and active listening is not about being quiet and waiting to respond like many people do.

​

  • It is being genuinely interested in what the person is saying.
  • It is being able to recount it back to the person speaking.
  • It is about asking great follow-up questions.
  • It is about remembering the next time you talk to the person.

​

Have you ever been in the presence of someone who is truly listening to you with 100% of the attention? Body language never lies, and you can feel it when someone genuinely cares and is listening to you.

​

I recently had the pleasure of speaking to Jim Alling (former President of Starbucks, COO of T-Mobile, and CEO of TOMS shoes).

​

In my very first Zoom conversation with Jim, he was all in. He gave me his undivided attention and was fully present. This is exceedingly rare, and this is why I consider active listening as a superpower that most people don’t have.

​

In our distracted society with all kinds of notifications going off on our devices becoming a great listener is a game-changing business partnership skill.

​

In addition to this, it builds trust which is critical to being an indispensable business partner.

​

Here are 7 ways to become a great active listener:

​

1) Active Engagement (nodding, eye contact, and verbal affirmations such as ‘Go on’).

​

2) Avoid Interruptions (wait for natural pauses to ask questions or provide feedback, showing respect for the speaker's thoughts and feelings).

​

3) Empathy and Open-mindedness (see to understand the speaker's perspective without immediate judgment or offering unsolicited advice).

​

4) Reflect and Clarify (paraphrase or summarize what the speaker has said to ensure they have correctly understood the message).

​

5) Nonverbal Cues (attentive to the speaker's nonverbal cues, such as tone of voice and body language, to understand context and nuances).

​

6) Distraction Management (minimize or eliminate distractions by putting away devices, choosing quiet environments, and focusing their attention solely on the speaker).

​

7) Feedback and Follow-Up (After listening, they provide thoughtful feedback or ask follow-up questions that show they have genuinely processed the information).

​

The FP&A Guy's Tech Tips

​

My tech tip for today is around FP&A Software. Over the weekend, I submitted the New & Improved 3rd Gen FP&A Tools Market Guide after nearly ten months of working on it. This year, for the guide, we did the following.

​

  • Had vendors submit 2 surveys
  • Conducted a customer survey
  • Conducted testing of the software
  • Conducted a founder story interview
  • Conducted a demo of each software tool.

​

This experience helped me gain a greater appreciation for how difficult it can be to select FP&A Software. When it comes to FP&A software, I am regularly asked what the best software is, and I always respond with the famous answer, "It Depends," but the reality is it depends on many things. That is why I regularly write about software in hopes of helping people better understand the marketplace. One of the graphs I often share is of the core pillars of FP&A software. I will be revamping this to be more of a pyramid at some point in the future but below is what I see as the core pillars of FP&A Software.

​

​

​

  • Data Management - FP&A software starts with the data layer. How does it bring in your data, what data does it bring in, how many dimensions can you have, how easy is it to create new metrics, etc.?
  • Modeling - Next is how flexible the tool is. Does it allow you to model your full business or will you still need to maintain a model in Excel? How robust is the calculation engine? Can it model both the financial and operational aspects of your business?
  • Dashboards/Reporting - What options does it have for building out dashboards and reports? Does it have the chart types you need? Can you easily comment on your reports and charts? How easy is it to modify the formatting of your charts?
  • Workflow/Collaboration - How does the tool manage the workflow and collaboration aspects of budgeting and forecasting? Is the tool one you can have your business partners use?
  • AI/ML - How does the vendor incorporate the use of AI/ML to make your life easier? Can you query your data using natural language processing? Will it build a predictive model using algorithms, etc? Each company takes a different approach to AI/ML, but it is important to understand how they think about this.

​

Start with Why by Simon Sinek

"Start with Why," by Simon Sinek, is a powerful exploration of how leaders can inspire action by first asking the fundamental question, "Why?" Sinek argues that understanding and communicating the purpose behind what we do is crucial for motivation and success. For Finance and Accounting teams, identifying their "Why" is pivotal in transforming routine tasks into meaningful contributions toward the organization's larger goals.

​

The book emphasizes the importance of the Golden Circle model, which starts with "Why" (the purpose), then "How" (the process), and finally "What" (the result). In the context of Finance and Accounting, the "Why" might relate to ensuring the financial health and sustainability of the organization, thereby enabling it to fulfill its mission and vision. Understanding this can help team members see beyond the numbers and connect their daily work to the larger impact of their roles.

​

​

For these teams, applying Sinek's principles means shifting the focus from simply completing financial reports or deliverables to understanding how these activities support strategic decision-making, foster organizational growth, and ensure ethical standards. This perspective helps in creating a more engaged and motivated team, as members understand their critical role in guiding the organization towards its objectives.

​

Leaders in Finance and Accounting can foster this understanding by regularly communicating how the team's work aligns with the organization's purpose and values. This not only enhances job satisfaction and productivity but also strengthens the team's cohesion and resilience in facing challenges, contributing to the organization's success by grounding their efforts in a meaningful "Why."

Spotlight Corner

Wassia Kamon

Wassia Kamon is a global FP&A influencer and superstar who continues to rise!

​

She lives in the USA and has taken the FP&A world by storm.

​

Wassia exudes positive energy and is such a great example of someone who genuinely loves what she does.

​

Wassia graduated from Georgia State University with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. Since then, she accumulated over a decade of progressive experience in corporate accounting and finance, with a focus on strategic planning, financial analysis, and business process improvements. She is also a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and a Certified Management Accountant (CMA), with a Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA). She currently serves as Vice President of Finance for Low Income Investment Fund.

Aside from work, Wassia enjoys gardening, cooking, and of course eating, while trying to keep up with her 2 young children. She believes that happiness is a choice and loves to spread positivity around her.

​

She was featured in a Wall Street Journal article and recently spoke at AFP 2023 with the topic being building and leading resilient teams.
